pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIGGER ADVENTURE

Same little dog. A little bigger adventure.

The Clown Club's Big Show was a big hit. Doc Leo got his costume back in the nick of time (thanks to a certain corgi), the crowd roared, and the whole Clown Club paraded through town until midnight with Teddy riding up front in THE CHEZ, Doc Leo's little red CitiCar, his head out of the window. Gwinn chased the confetti. Everybody went home happy and tired.

Well. Almost everybody.

In the morning, Gwinn's bed is empty. Her pink collar is gone. So is Doc Leo's rubber chicken. A trail of confetti leads out the doggy door.

And Doc Leo has news: the Clown Club is booked at the Tri-County Fair tonight, way out past the river. The Big Show was big. This show is bigger. Teddy is the opening act.

Teddy will not go anywhere without his big sister. (He will not say so. But he keeps looking at her bed.) So Doc Leo drives THE CHEZ, and Teddy does the sniffing: across town, over the river, through a corn maze and out to the Fair, fetching whatever Gwinn dropped along the way so Doc Leo knows where to drive next.

And where is Gwinn while all this goes on? Every so often the story says MEANWHILE... and then you are Gwinn.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY2 and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, boofs and sniffs; without one, the PC speaker does its best.

A cartoon plays first (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key for the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around Doc Leo's house himself.

There are nine stops. Before each one, a card shows which stop it is (LEVEL 2 OF 9), where you are, what to look for, and what is new. At the end of each of Teddy's stops, Doc Leo waits beside THE CHEZ, plugged in at a charger (its charge port is low on the back, on the passenger side). His thought bubble shows what Gwinn dropped there: bring it to him, the car door pops open, and you're off. At the end of Gwinn's stops, hop onto her ride.

Energy and naps

Teddy (and Gwinn) start with 100 energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests and flying things wear a dog down, and the Fair's bees, popcorn and practice pies sting the most; bones give 25 back, and they get scarcer the farther from home you go. When energy runs out it's nap time, and you wake at the start of the stop. When the naps are all used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Moving and Hopping
pages.html:
Moving and Hopping

Left Right
or A D		Walk. Gwinn walks faster. Gwinn does everything faster.
Up or WHop! Hold it to hop higher, let go to steer. Gwinn hops higher than Teddy (she is twice his size).
Q EHop up and to the left (Q) or right (E) in one go: the way across stepping stones and over skunks.

Ledges

Awnings, shelves, stairs, branches, the gazebo roof, hay bale steps and the floors of the corn maze can be hopped up through from below and stood on from above. A hole in a floor drops you through; trot fast and you may skim right over a small one.

Things that lift and carry

Doc Leo's bed bounces. The bucket truck's bucket, the mill's grain hoist, the carousel horses and THE BIG DROP ride up and down: step on and hold still. The hay elevator's belt carries Gwinn up to the loft. Rapids carry a swimming dog downstream; the pool and the pig wallow just hold you up.

Wind

At the Fair it is windy. Where you see streaks in the air, a breeze carries Gwinn along: walk into it, or hop up into it, and let it take her across. A fan lying face up blows her straight up. Up on the roofs the gusts come and go: watch the windsocks. When they stand straight out, a gust is blowing; when they hang limp, it's calm, so run for the next vent before they lift again.

pages.head: Teddy's Tricks
pages.html:
Teddy's Tricks

Teddy still knows a ton of tricks, and he learned a new one.

SSniff. New! Look for a faint wisp hanging in the air: a scent. Stand by it and sniff, and whatever is hidden there turns up: treats, a bone, a balloon dog, the thing Gwinn dropped, or Gwinn's paw prints pointing the way she went.
SpaceSpeak. WOOF! Dust bunnies, mice, pigeons, ducks and one very groomed poodle clear out.
DownDig. Bones sticking out of the ground, soft dirt with paw prints.
FFetch. Pick up what you're standing on.
1High five. And now: ring the bell. Teddy rings a bell with his paw. Watch where the DING goes: a rung bell drops its ding onto whatever hangs below it, and things start happening.
2Sit pretty. A heart floats up and wins over anybody with a SIT? bubble. Also useful for teaching by example.
3Spin. For turnstiles and anybody asking to see a SPIN?
4Play dead. Hold it: flat as a rug, and popcorn flies right over.

Roll over? Teddy has retired from rolling over, by choice, the same way he retired from hoops. He is a professional now.

pages.head: Gwinn's Tricks
pages.html:
Gwinn's Tricks

In the MEANWHILE... stops you are Gwinn: a chocolate pit-lab mix with amber eyes and a pink collar, younger than Teddy and twice his size. She has tricks of her own.

SpaceBOOF. A big bark that rolls a long way: raccoons, chickens, crows, goats, geese.
DownDig big. Through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.
1Chew. Ropes, knots, gates tied shut.
2Sit. She is still learning. She gets about halfway, sits for one moment, and is up again wiggling. (It does nothing. Yet.)
3Zoomies! A brown blur there and back that bowls over boxes and hay bales on both sides.
4Flop. Hold it: she lies down like she owns the place, and owls (and pies) sail right over.

She fetches (F) too. She is very good at fetching. She is less good at giving things back.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats and bones

Dog biscuits are everywhere, 10 points each (the F2 screen counts them as Money). A bone gives back 25 energy.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's balloon animals: a few bob somewhere up high in every stop, 250 points and 10 energy each. Some hide in scents.

What Gwinn dropped

Doc Leo's househer pink collar
Main Streether pink rope leash
The riverDoc Leo's rubber chicken
The corn mazea corn dog stick, licked clean
The midwayher dog show entry card (number 13)
The dog showa blue ribbon, if she earns one

Fair tickets

The Clown Club's booths on the midway pay a ticket for a good trick. THE BIG DROP's gate takes three. The F2 screen shows how many you have.

The Dog House

The tiny red library on Maple Street is still there, and its paw-knob drawer still has snacks. Something smells interesting in its rock cubby.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Friends

  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club. Chewed felt fedora, wire glasses, purple shirt, green tie, blue suspenders, corduroy jacket, and a rubber chicken on a leash (when he can find it). Always orders root beer.
  • THE CHEZ: his little red 1976 CitiCar, 100% electric. It charges at about a mile an hour, so it stops at every charger it sees.
  • The Town Crier: rings in Founders' Day on the Commons in his tricorn and linen hunting shirt. Early mornings are not his best time.
  • The miller: runs the old mill on the river. Won't run the hoist for a dog who hasn't been polite.
  • Honker, Bubbles, Twirly and Professor Pratfall: the Clown Club, working the Fair's booths. At noon Honker keeps the dog show's sign-up sheet, and Pratfall practices his pie throws (for science).
  • Juggles: the Clown Club's juggler, practicing by the trailer on the back lot.
  • The judge: of the Best Behaved class. Has seen a lot of dogs. Has not seen Gwinn.

Pests and nuisances

  • Dust bunnies, mice, pigeons, ducks: bark.
  • Raccoons, crows, chickens, goats, geese: BOOF.
  • The skunk: do not BOOF. Hop.
  • Spiders, owls, popcorn, practice pies, bees, the fisherman's hook: keep clear, or flop, or play dead.
  • The rival poodle: very groomed. Very unimpressed. Bark.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's House

Three floors and a basement, cut open like a dollhouse. Bark the dust bunny, get over the fridge by way of the counter, and drop through the laundry chute's hole to the basement: Gwinn's collar is in the laundry basket. Sniff. Then up the stairs and out the doggy door to THE CHEZ.

2. Main Street

Founders' Day! Gwinn's leash is tangled round the gazebo's weathervane. Ring the bucket truck's bell, ride its bucket up and step onto the roof. (Ring the Town Crier's bell, too: he has news.)

3. Meanwhile: Gwinn's Night Out

Last night, after the parade. Gwinn chews through the back gate's rope, BOOFs a raccoon, crosses the park by lamplight, knocks a pile of boxes flat, digs under the playground fence, gets past a skunk and hops into the Clown Club's hay wagon, bound for the Fair.

4. The River

Hop the stepping stones over the rapids, sit pretty for the miller, ride his grain hoist up to the loft, cross the high bank and swim out into the pool for the rubber chicken going round the eddy.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

5. Meanwhile: Gwinn on the Farm

The hay wagon stopped at a farm at dawn. So many chickens (she thinks they're all Doc Leo's rubber chicken). The hay elevator carries her up into the barn loft; zoomies flatten the bales; she wades through the pig wallow, BOOFs the goat, chews the gate's rope and hops into a Ferris wheel car riding to the Fair.

6. The Corn Maze

Three tiers of paths through the corn. Hay bales are steps up; holes drop you down. Sniff the scents and follow Gwinn's paw prints to the scarecrow at the heart of the maze, where she left a corn dog stick.

7. Meanwhile: Gwinn Signs Up

Noon on the Fair's back lot, before the gates open, and it is windy. BOOF the geese, ride the big fan's breeze along the Clown Club's costume line, and flop under Professor Pratfall's practice pies. Hop into the breeze over the creek (fall in and the current brings you back to try again), and let a fan lying face up lift you onto the roofs. Then back the other way into the wind, vent to vent, to the bandstand, where Honker has the sign-up sheet.

8. The Fair Midway

Earn tickets with tricks at the Clown Club's booths and climb the High Striker to ring its bell. Three tickets get you onto THE BIG DROP, twenty-one blocks straight up, where Gwinn's entry card blew. (Hop onto the trampoline by Twirly's wheel, too: it bounces you up to a perch of treats.)

9. The Dog Show

Every trick you know: spin the turnstile, climb the A-frame, go round the hoop, play dead under the popcorn, bark the rival poodle off between pops from the second popcorn stand, ring the judges' bell. And then there's Gwinn in the Best Behaved ring, and a judge saying SIT.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits

Design, art, music and programming: Claude, for Sandbox Software.

Yankee Doodle (the fife on Main Street) is a traditional American tune from the 1700s, in the public domain; the arrangement is the game's own.

Starring Teddy as himself, a little bigger this time. Gwinn as herself (sorry, everybody). Doc Leo, still the friendliest hobo clown in any clown club, and THE CHEZ, his red 1976 CitiCar. No dogs were rushed. Gwinn did her own stunts, and some of everybody else's.

Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs. No programming needed!

news.head: Teddy's back, and this time Gwinn's playable
news.html: Our corgi's sequel, Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure, is out! Nine levels from the attic to the dog show, a brand-new trick (SNIFF), and the first Sandbox game with two heroes: in the MEANWHILE... levels you are Gwinn, with tricks of her own. One of them is sitting. She is working on it.

news.head: Since last issue: The kingdom got around to it
news.html: Quest for the Round Tuit players have been very prompt. The Royal Library reports the Tome of Tomorrow returned, three hundred years overdue, by dozens of you, and Doc Leo reports Sir Reginald Cluckington III home safe. The most-asked question on the BBS: where can I swim? Nowhere. The rivers of Procrastia can't be swum. Look for bridges.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Gwinn's progress report
news.html: Gwinn has her own levels this time, and our testers say she's a natural: she BOOFs, she chews, she digs big and she does zoomies straight through the hay bales. Her SIT is coming along. She gets about halfway, sits for one moment, and is up again wiggling. We're told that's how it starts.

news.head: In the workshop: The biggest one yet
news.html: The Clown Club is putting a band together for the town parade, and Gwinn has already knocked over the trunk: Tune-Up is next, with thirteen neighborhoods of lost instruments for Teddy to fetch. Then the Teddy trilogy ends with Teddy's Little Biggest Adventure: every place from the first two games, more heroes than ever, and, for the first time, you get to drive THE CHEZ. What's the occasion? We can't say. Gwinn made us promise.

news.head: Letters: "Why did Teddy stop rolling over?"
news.html: He retired from it, by choice, like he retired from hoops. He is a professional now. Roll over's key went to his new SNIFF, which our testers say is the best trick in the game. Teddy agrees.

items.title: Teddy & Gwinn Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. One answer at a time: Teddy believes in you. Gwinn believes in corn dogs.

hints.q: What is that faint wispy thing in the air?
hints.a: A scent! Stand next to it and press S to sniff. Whatever is hidden there turns up: treats, a bone, a balloon dog, paw prints, and sometimes exactly what you are looking for.

hints.q: I found the thing Gwinn dropped. Now what?
hints.a: Bring it to Doc Leo at THE CHEZ, his little red car, at the end of the stop. Its door opens for it: hop in and he drives on.

hints.q: How do Gwinn's levels end?
hints.a: She is following her nose to the Fair. Look for her ride at the end: the hay wagon, then the Fair's ride truck. Hop in. At the Fair itself, she is headed for the dog show's sign-up table.

hints.q: Where is Gwinn's collar?
hints.a: She slipped out of it down the laundry chute. Drop through the hole in the laundry room floor, land in the basket in the basement and sniff (S).

hints.q: How do I get over the fridge?
hints.a: Hop onto the kitchen counter first, then up onto the fridge, then down the other side.

hints.q: How do I get out of the basement?
hints.a: The stairs at the back go up to the laundry room: hop from step to step. Then out the doggy door.

hints.q: What is in the attic?
hints.a: Bounce on Doc Leo's bed upstairs: it sends you up through the hatch. A balloon dog and a lot of boxes marked WIGS.

hints.q: Gwinn's leash is on top of the gazebo!
hints.a: Ring the bucket truck's bell (high five, 1) beside the gazebo. Its bucket starts going up and down: ride it up, step onto the roof and fetch (F) the leash from the weathervane.

hints.q: The Town Crier is asleep on his feet.
hints.a: Ring his bell with a high five. He calls out the news and drops a proclamation worth five treats.

hints.q: Pigeons keep pecking me.
hints.a: Bark (Space) first.

hints.q: The back gate won't open.
hints.a: It's tied with rope. Gwinn chews (1).

hints.q: A pile of boxes blocks the path.
hints.a: Zoomies (3) knock it flat. Chewing won't, and boofing won't.

hints.q: The playground fence is too tall.
hints.a: Dig big (Down) at its foot: Gwinn's dig goes through hard clay Teddy couldn't scratch.

hints.q: There's a skunk.
hints.a: Do NOT boof at it. Wait until it waddles toward you, then hop over it (E).

hints.q: I keep falling in the rapids.
hints.a: No harm done: the current carries you to the mill bank. Hop the stones with E, or let the water take you.

hints.q: How do I get past the mill?
hints.a: The miller wants a sit. Sit pretty (2) near him: his OK drops onto the grain hoist and it starts. Ride it up to the loft and out the door.

hints.q: Where is the rubber chicken?
hints.a: Going round and round in the pool below the high bank. Jump in and swim to it.

hints.q: How does Gwinn get into the barn loft?
hints.a: Walk onto the hay elevator's belt: it carries her up and through the loft floor.

hints.q: The bales won't budge.
hints.a: Zoomies (3).

hints.q: The goat is in the way.
hints.a: BOOF (Space) at it, then chew (1) the rope on the gate.

hints.q: Which way?
hints.a: Sniff the scents (S): each becomes Gwinn's paw prints pointing the way she went. Hay bales are steps up; holes in a floor drop you down (and you can't climb back).

hints.q: Where's the thing she dropped?
hints.a: At the heart of the maze, by the scarecrow, on the top tier. Sniff there.

hints.q: The creek is too wide to hop.
hints.a: Stand by the fan on the bank and hop up into its breeze (E): it carries Gwinn right across. Fall in, and the current brings her back to the bank to try again.

hints.q: How do I get up to the bandstand?
hints.a: Not from the ground. Keep going right, past the poultry barn, to the fan lying face up: step on it and it blows Gwinn up onto the roof. The way back to the bandstand is over the roofs.

hints.q: The wind keeps blowing me back!
hints.a: Watch the windsocks. Wait behind a vent while they stand out; when they hang limp, run for the next vent. A gust never hurts, it only pushes.

hints.q: How do I earn tickets?
hints.a: Tricks! Climb the High Striker's pegs and high five its bell; sit pretty for Bubbles at the ring toss; spin for Twirly at the wheel; sniff by the carousel.

hints.q: THE BIG DROP won't let me on.
hints.a: Its gate takes three tickets. With three, walk through it, hop on the car at the bottom and ride to the top. Gwinn's entry card is on the deck.

hints.q: The popcorn keeps hitting me.
hints.a: Play dead (hold 4) as it comes: it flies right over. There are two stands, and the second pops right past the rival poodle, so bark at her between pops.

hints.q: How do I get into the Best Behaved ring?
hints.a: Ring the bell on the judges' table (high five). The velvet rope comes down.

hints.q: Gwinn won't sit!
hints.a: Show her how. Stand under the judge's SIT? and sit pretty (2) yourself. She sits! For three whole seconds.

hints.q: Gwinn has a secret spot. Everybody knows that. Nobody knows where.
hints.a: Somewhere you'd never walk on Main Street. Have you ever just kept going the wrong way?

hints.q: Where does the wrong way go?
hints.a: Town is smaller than it looks. Walk LEFT from The Dog House, past the end of Maple Street, and keep walking: you come out behind the tall hedge at the far end of town.

hints.q: Dig where, exactly?
hints.a: Behind the hedge, past the sign that says MINE and the bone sticking out of the lawn, there's soft dirt with paw prints. Dig (Down), step into the hole and you drop into Gwinn's den. Fetch the egg (F) from her loot pile, then climb out on the right.

items.title: The Corn Maze Postcard and Grille
items.note: Lay the card over the postcard to read the way through
items.heading: GREETINGS FROM THE TRI-COUNTY FAIR
items.caption: The Corn Maze
howto: Gwinn's postcard is full of plain news about the Fair. Cut out the grille card (glue its two faces back to back) and cut its four numbered holes.

The grille has two pictures on its edges: a corn dog and a paw print. Slide, turn and flip the card until each picture looks straight out along its row or column, to the same picture printed on the postcard.
Read the holes in number order. BALE means hop up a hay bale step; HOLE means drop down a hole. Most places read nonsense, and a few read a wrong way through the maze.

puzzles.ask: The Corn Maze: three tiers of paths between the corn, and some paths only end. Which way up and down is the real way through?
puzzles.answer: Bale, bale, hole, hole: up two hay bale steps, then down two holes.

2.long: Stand up and slap whatever is just above and ahead: balloons, a held-out hand.

3.long: Send up a heart that floats two blocks. Anybody asking SIT! is won over.

4.long: Twirl a whirlwind to each side. Turns revolving doors and turnstiles.

5.long: Hold to flop flat as a rug, so things fly over Teddy.

16.long: Hop up and to the left in one go.

17.long: Hop. Same as Up: tap for a little hop, hold to hop higher.

18.long: Hop up and to the right in one go.

30.long: Walk left (same as the Left arrow).

31.long: Sniff out what is hidden where you see a faint wisp.

32.long: Walk right (same as the Right arrow).

33.long: Pick up something lying where Teddy stands, such as one of Doc Leo's costume pieces.

57.long: Bark. WOOF! scares off pests. (Gwinn's BOOF is a bigger bark.)

72.long: Hop. Tap for a little hop, hold to hop higher; let go to steer.

75.long: Walk left. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.

77.long: Walk right. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.

80.long: Dig up the block under Teddy's feet: bones, or soft dirt that gives way to a tunnel.

1.long: Bark. WOOF! scares off squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese.

2.long: Stand up and slap whatever is just above and ahead.
